speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the consultation. I see you are a newborn with a generalized rash; can you tell me exactly when this rash first appeared on your skin?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. The rash began today in a 4-day-old term infant with a mother who had untreated prenatal care but treated gonorrhea four years ago. Is the rash associated with any fever, poor feeding, or lethargy?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Gonococcal Sepsis (Disseminated Gonococcal Infection).

The presence of pustules on an erythematous base, sparing the palms and soles, in a 4-day-old infant is highly characteristic of disseminated gonococcal infection, despite the mother's past treatment for gonorrhea. I am requesting results for a Gram stain and culture of the pustular lesions.
